items.title: AI in Finance: From Automation to Intelligence
items.venue: DKTE Society's Yashwantrao Chavan Polytechnic, Ichalkaranji
items.summary:
Conducted an interactive seminar for 300+ Engineering & AI students, exploring Generative AI, automation, governance and vibe coding.

Key Takeaway: AI is not just a technology to understand—it is a capability to apply, innovate and build real-world solutions.
items.description:
As a Chartered Accountant, my journey into AI began with a simple question: How can technology make the knowledge and skills we already have more powerful?

That curiosity took me from finance and accounting into AI, automation and technology. Being able to bring that journey to the next generation of engineers and AI professionals was deeply meaningful.

I had the opportunity to conduct an expert seminar for 300+ Engineering and AI-stream students, exploring Generative AI, LLMs, prompting, Agentic AI, workflow automation, AI governance, responsible AI and vibe coding.

Through live demonstrations and practical examples, we explored how AI can move beyond being a tool we use to becoming a new way of thinking, solving problems and building possibilities.

What stayed with me most was a message from a student after the session asking how he could start building Agentic AI himself and what he should learn.

That, to me, was the real outcome of the session—not just sharing knowledge but sparking curiosity that continues after the room goes quiet.

Key Takeaway
The future belongs not merely to those who know AI, but to those who are curious enough to experiment, courageous enough to build, and thoughtful enough to use it responsibly.

items.title: AI Quick Crash Course with live demonstration
items.venue: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), Ichalkaranji Branch, (WIRC)
items.summary: Conducted an AI Quick Crash Course for Chartered Accountants at ICAI Ichalkaranji Branch, WIRC, combining live AI demonstrations, VBA automation and practical AI governance frameworks to help professionals move from AI awareness to confident, responsible adoption.
items.description:
I had the opportunity to conduct an AI Quick Crash Course for members of the ICAI Ichalkaranji Branch, WIRC—a session designed not merely to introduce AI tools, but to show professionals what becomes possible when AI is applied to real professional work.

Through live demonstrations, practical prompting, workflow automation and VBA scripting, we explored how AI can help professionals automate repetitive tasks, work with data, create practical solutions and enhance everyday productivity.

The session also brought AI governance into the conversation, covering AI Policy, AI Inventory & Risk Assessment, privacy considerations, a 6-Document Professional Firm Pack, and a project-level 12-Gate AI Screening Checklist.

The emphasis throughout was on a balanced approach:

Experiment with AI. Build with AI. But govern it responsibly.

For me, the most valuable part of the session was demonstrating that AI fluency is not about collecting a list of tools—it is about developing the judgement to identify opportunities, the skills to build solutions, and the discipline to manage the risks.
